info.title: CalMonkey API
info.summary: One calendar API for Google, Microsoft and Apple iCloud.
info.description:
Read and write your users' Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, Outlook.com and Apple iCloud calendars through one API: hosted connect pages, calendars, free/busy, events with guests, repeating events and meeting links, and signed webhooks.

Field names and shapes are the ones existing calendar integrations already use (see /docs/compatibility).

Documentation: https://calmonkey.com/docs (as Markdown: https://calmonkey.com/llms.txt).

get.description: Opened in the user's browser, not called by your server. The user picks a calendar provider, signs in with it and comes back to redirect_uri with ?code=…&state=…, or with ?error=access_denied when they cancel or decline. An unknown client id or a redirect URI that is not registered shows an error page and never redirects.

servers.description: The app host: what people see in a browser.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Always code.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Your application's client id.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: One of the application's redirect URIs, exactly as registered.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Defaults to read_write.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Any value; it comes back unchanged.

parameters.name: provider_name
parameters.description: Skip the chooser: google, office365, live_connect or apple.

parameters.name: link_token
parameters.description: From POST /v1/link_tokens: the calendar account connected in this run joins that account.

302.description: On to the calendar provider, or back to redirect_uri with code or error.

400.description: An error page: the client id is unknown or the redirect URI is not registered for it.

post.summary: Exchange a code for tokens, or refresh an access token
post.description: grant_type authorization_code needs client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri. grant_type refresh_token needs client_id, client_secret and refresh_token; its response has no sub, account_id or linking_profile. Access tokens last 3 hours; the refresh token does not change.

400.description: invalid_client (wrong client id or secret), invalid_grant (code used, expired or for another redirect URI; refresh token revoked), invalid_request (a field is missing) or unsupported_grant_type.

post.description: Needs client_id, client_secret and token (an access or a refresh token). Revokes the whole grant: every token of the account stops working, its channels close, and its stored provider credentials and cached events are deleted. An application calendar is deleted with it.

200.description: Empty body, whether or not the token was known.

post.description: A calendar hosted by CalMonkey, opened with your client credentials alone: no user and no browser. Creates the calendar on first use and returns tokens for it; the same application_calendar_id always opens the same calendar. The account has one profile and one writable, primary calendar. Needs client_id, client_secret and application_calendar_id.

200.description: Tokens for the calendar's account (sub is apc_…).

get.description: For an application calendar of an application in compatibility mode the answer is 403 with a plain-text body.

403.description: An application calendar, in compatibility mode.

get.summary: Who the token belongs to, with every connected profile and its calendars
get.description: The type and data are under calmonkey.type and calmonkey.data (in compatibility mode, under the key names existing integrations read).

200.description: The account, its profiles and their calendars.

get.summary: The calendar accounts the user connected
get.description: profile_connected false means the person has to connect that calendar account again: send them through /oauth/authorize with the same provider_name.

200.description: The profiles, each with its calendars.

get.description: The same shape for every provider. Write to calendars whose calendar_readonly is false. Calendars deleted at the provider stay in the list with calendar_deleted true.

One period per event (one per occurrence of a repeating event). Events your application wrote are left out unless include_managed=true. Up to 1,000 periods per page: follow pages.next_page, an absolute URL, as it is.

parameters.name: tzid
parameters.description: Time zone the request's dates are read in, e.g. Australia/Melbourne.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: a day (2026-11-03) in tzid, or a time with an offset. Defaults to 42 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End, exclusive. Defaults to 201 days from now.

parameters.name: calendar_ids[]
parameters.description: Only these calendars (up to 100), sent as calendar_ids[]=a&calendar_ids[]=b. Default: every calendar of the account.

parameters.name: include_managed
parameters.description: Include the events this application created through the API. Default false.

parameters.name: include_ids
parameters.description: Add event_id to the periods of events this application created.

parameters.name: localized_times
parameters.description: Times with the offset of tzid instead of UTC.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a later page. Do not build it: follow pages.next_page as it is.

200.description: The busy, tentative and free periods.

get.description: Every event in the account's calendars from 42 days back to 201 days ahead, with guests, their replies and meeting links. A repeating event is returned as its occurrences. Events your application wrote are left out unless include_managed=true. Up to 300 events per page: follow pages.next_page.

parameters.name: tzid
parameters.description: Time zone the request's dates are read in, e.g. Australia/Melbourne.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: a day (2026-11-03) in tzid, or a time with an offset. Defaults to 42 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End, exclusive. Defaults to 201 days from now.

parameters.name: calendar_ids[]

parameters.name: include_managed

parameters.name: only_managed
parameters.description: Only the events this application created.

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Include events deleted since they were cached (deleted: true).

parameters.name: localized_times

post.description: Creates the event with this event_id, or replaces it: sending the same body twice leaves one event. attendees invites guests, recurrence makes the event repeat and conferencing adds the calendar's own meeting link. The event is in GET /v1/events and /v1/free_busy as soon as the 202 is sent; the write to the calendar provider follows. Fields the API does not have are accepted and ignored.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The calendar (cal_…), from GET /v1/calendars.

delete.summary: Delete an event, or one occurrence of a repeating event
delete.description: The body names the event by the event_id it was written with. Without occurrence_date a repeating event is deleted with all its occurrences. Also 202 when there is no such event.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The calendar (cal_…), from GET /v1/calendars.

post.summary: Change one occurrence of a repeating event
post.description: Gives one occurrence of a repeating event your application wrote its own time, text or both, without sending the series again. The body is everything that differs for this occurrence: it replaces an earlier change of the same occurrence. At least one of a new start and end, summary, description and location is needed.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The calendar (cal_…), from GET /v1/calendars.

post.description: CalMonkey POSTs a signed notification to callback_url whenever the account's calendars change; a verification notification is sent at once. signing_secret is returned only here. An account has at most 100 open channels. Changes your application made through the API are never notified back to it.

get.description: Filters that were not set are left out.

delete.description: Also 202 when the channel was already closed.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: The channel (chn_…).

404.description: An id the account never had.

post.summary: Get a link token, to add another calendar account to this account
post.description: Pass it to /oauth/authorize as link_token: the calendar account connected in that run joins the account this access token belongs to. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

post.summary: What CalMonkey POSTs to a channel's callback URL
post.description: Answer with any 2xx within 5 seconds. Anything else, a redirect included, is retried for about 23 hours; 410 closes the channel. Verify the signature over the raw body before trusting it.

parameters.name: Calmonkey-HMAC-SHA256
parameters.description: Base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with your client secret. During a secret rotation, one value per active secret, comma-separated.

parameters.name: Calmonkey-Signature
parameters.description: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>"> keyed with the channel's whsec_ secret. Not sent to applications in compatibility mode.

parameters.name: Calmonkey-Delivery-Id
parameters.description: whd_…: the same on every retry of one notification.

parameters.name: Calmonkey-Delivery-Attempt
parameters.description: 1 for the first attempt.

410.description: Close the channel: no more notifications are sent to it.

accessToken.description: An account's access token (cmat_…), from POST /oauth/token or POST /v1/application_calendars. Valid for 3 hours; get a new one with the refresh token. The OAuth endpoints and POST /v1/application_calendars take your client id and client secret in the request body instead.

Calmonkey-Request-Id.description: Identifies the request. Send your own in the request's Calmonkey-Request-Id header and it comes back unchanged.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The burst size of the tighter of the two rate-limit buckets (per application, per access token).

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until that bucket is full again.

Unauthorized.description: The access token is missing, expired or revoked. Empty body. Refresh the token and retry once.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bearer realm="calmonkey", error="invalid_token" (or "invalid_request" when no token was sent), error_description="…"

ReadOnly.description: The calendar is read-only. Empty body.

NotFound.description: A calendar the account does not have (or, on the occurrences endpoint, an event_id your application has not written to it). Empty body.

ValidationError.description: The request is invalid, or asks for something the calendar cannot do. Nothing was written.

RateLimited.description: Over a rate limit. Empty body. Wait Retry-After seconds, then retry.

code.description: With grant_type authorization_code: the code from the callback. Valid once, for 10 minutes.

redirect_uri.description: With grant_type authorization_code: the redirect URI the authorization request used.

refresh_token.description: With grant_type refresh_token: the account's refresh token.

expires_in.description: Seconds the access token is valid for: 10800 (3 hours).

refresh_token.description: Gets new access tokens. Does not change.

sub.description: The account: acc_… (apc_… for an application calendar). Not in a refresh response.

series_identifier.description: On every occurrence of a repeating event: the same value for all occurrences of one series.

occurrence_date.description: On an occurrence of a repeating event: its original day in the series' time zone (YYYY-MM-DD).

event_id.description: Your id for the event. Unique per calendar and application: writing it again replaces the event.

start.description: A time with an offset (2026-11-03T03:00:00Z), a date for an all-day event, or { "time": "…", "tzid": "…" }.

end.description: As start: a date when start is a date (exclusive), a time when start is a time, not before start.

tzid.description: The event's time zone, e.g. Australia/Melbourne. Needed for a repeating event with a time.

transparency.description: opaque (busy, the default) or transparent (shown as free).

attendees.description: A change to the event's guests, not the whole list: the guests after the write are the guests it had, plus invite, minus remove.

notify_attendees.description: Whether the calendar tells the guests about this write. Default true.

interval.description: Every how many days, weeks, months or years. Default 1.

count.description: How many occurrences in all, the first included. Not together with until.

until.description: The last day an occurrence may fall on (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, in the event's time zone). Not together with count.

add.description: Days to skip, each an occurrence's original day (YYYY-MM-DD).

change.description: Occurrences with a time or text of their own, each named by its original day.

recurrence.description: How the event repeats: one rule, and exceptions. null stops it repeating; left out, a series stays as it is.

profile_id.description: default (add the calendar's own link where it has one), integrated (the same, and 422 on a calendar that has none) or none (take the link off).

conferencing.description: Asks the calendar to add its own meeting link, or to take it off.

event_id.description: The id the event was written with.

occurrence_date.description: Cancel only this occurrence of a repeating event: its original day in the event's time zone (YYYY-MM-DD).

notify_attendees.description: Whether guests are sent the cancellation. Default true.

event_id.description: The id the series was written with.

occurrence_date.description: The occurrence's original day in the event's time zone (YYYY-MM-DD).

tzid.description: The time zone of the new time. Default: the series' own.

notify_attendees.description: Whether guests are told. Default true.

callback_url.description: Where notifications are POSTed: https, port 443, a public host, no credentials in the URL.

key.description: What is wrong, e.g. errors.required. Match on this.

ValidationError.description: Every field with a problem, by its path in the request (start, location.description, calendar_ids[0]; base for the whole body), each with a list of { key, description }. Keys: errors.required, errors.invalid, errors.invalid_type, errors.invalid_format, errors.invalid_value, errors.too_small, errors.too_big, errors.invalid_json, errors.invalid_callback_url, errors.invalid_callback_url_blocked, errors.too_many_channels, errors.invalid_email, errors.too_many_attendees, errors.attendees_unsupported, errors.notify_attendees_unsupported, errors.conferencing_unavailable, errors.max_recurrence_rules_exceeded, errors.not_recognized, errors.not_supported, errors.must_be_integer_greater_than_zero, errors.must_be_date, errors.not_supported_count_until_combination, errors.not_recurring, errors.not_an_occurrence. Applications in compatibility mode get the wording existing integrations expect, with these keys in place of ours: errors.tzid_unrecognized, errors.invalid_time_pair, errors.event.cannot_set_attendees, errors.integrated_conferencing_not_available.
